open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct, or refute by a specific encoded experiment, a finite shared-trace recession library satisfying canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate, simultaneous-collar compatibility, translated-uniform tails, and an input-computable refinement schedule with vanishing accumulated error.
open_obligations.obstruction: The available active-set geometry controls only forward motion from a fixed mean. It does not prove that canonical sections throughout protected stars preserve every active semantic region and the separated-risk set. Equality of shared mesh vertices on a geometric face does not control the actual face--cone candidates throughout simultaneous collar supports. No translated-uniform guard and normal-base tail bound or explicit refinement-count recurrence has been derived. Hence the standing assumptions currently support neither an affirmative construction nor a negative encoded-experiment witness.
open_obligations.attempted: The prior construction used one smoothed ancestor, one common rational simplicial fan, common raywise Følner factors, and shared finite-element face variables. This gives path-independent operators and explicit translation-boundary ratios. The proposed collar induction is circular if its traces are defined from the already-glued rule, while constant lower-skeleton extension can assign positive weight to an unsafe candidate. Per-cell bounds also cannot be summed without controlling the growing refinement count. In accordance with the directive after this barrier was isolated, no further generic averaging reroll was used.

prose_updates.tldr: The unconditional contribution consists of three proved pieces: common-ray Foelner operators are path-independent and have explicit translation-boundary ratios; Carter's bounded-ratio kernels give fixed-base compact multinomial transfer with separately displayed semantic, covariance, and \(C_{2/\kappa}m\log(m)/\sqrt n\) charges; and compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit together with two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows, but no global upper limit. Replayable moving-offset transfer and CertGluePFL termination remain conditional on a separately supplied finite compatibility package satisfying the five certificates listed in the open-ended question.
